bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to consumer protection; limiting the import, manufacture, or sale of certain table saws; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 325E.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[325E.0685] TABLE SAWS; SAFETY REQUIREMENT.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Entity" means a corporation, limited liability company, partnership, or other organization authorized to transact business in Minnesota. Entity does not include any state or local government unit.

(c) "Table saw" means a woodworking tool that has a motor-driven circular saw blade that protrudes through the surface of a table and is powered by alternating current from a wall outlet. Table saw includes but is not limited to a bench, job site, contractor, hybrid, cabinet, or sliding saw.

(d) "Test probe" means a device that enables the accurate measurement of the depth of a cut. Test probe does not include a finger or other human body part.

Subd. 2.

Prohibition.

(a) An entity must not import, manufacture, sell, or offer for sale a table saw that the entity knows or has reason to know does not meet the requirements under paragraph (b).

(b) The maximum depth a table saw is capable of cutting for a test probe must not exceed 3.5 millimeters when the table saw:

(1) is powered on;

(2) has the center axis of a test probe moving parallel to, with a tolerance of 13 millimeters to 17 millimeters, above the tabletop at a rate of one meter per second; and

(3) has the test probe contact a spinning saw blade that is set at the maximum height setting.

Subd. 3.

Exception.

An entity does not violate this section if the entity is unable to obtain, on fair, reasonable, and nondiscriminatory terms, a license under a patent required to comply with subdivision 2.

Subd. 4.

Enforcement.

An entity that violates this section is subject to the penalties and remedies, including a private right of action to recover damages, as provided in section 8.31.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective January 1, 2027.
